Name: belief_commitment_onset
Title: The Moment of Commitment: Locating When an LLM's Belief About an Item Crystallizes During Reading
Short Hypothesis: As an LLM reads a proposition token-by-token, its internal belief about the item's truth-value is not fixed but crystallizes at an identifiable 'commitment point' along the token stream; we hypothesize that (a) this commitment onset is measurable via token-wise probing of a truth direction, (b) premature commitment (before the disambiguating/final token is read) predicts belief-vs-fact errors and shallow-heuristic answering, and (c) causally delaying commitment by suppressing the truth direction until the proposition is fully read reduces such errors without harming factual QA.
Related Work: Suzgun et al. ('Belief in the Machine'/KaBLE) and the referenced 'Language models cannot reliably distinguish belief from knowledge and fact' establish behavioral belief/knowledge/fact conflation but treat belief as a single one-shot judgment read out at the end of the prompt. Truth-direction probing (Marks & Tegmark; Savcisens & Eliassi-Rad 'Trilemma of Truth'; Schouten et al. on context-sensitivity) recovers a static veracity axis, typically read at the final token. My prior proposals covered agent-attribution, evidence-update inertia, item-truth binding, temporal indexing, provenance, graded strength, logical coherence, operative-vs-avowed introspection, and suppositional framing. NONE study the *within-proposition temporal dynamics* of belief formation — i.e., at which token the model commits to a truth-value and whether committing too early (before reading the fact-determining token) causes errors. This recasts belief-vs-fact confusion as a premature-commitment / reading-dynamics problem, a genuinely new lens.
Abstract: Existing probing work reads an LLM's belief about a proposition from the final token, treating belief as a static endpoint. But belief forms incrementally as the model reads: consider 'The Great Wall of China is visible from the Moon' — does the model commit to a truth-value before or after reading the crucial word 'Moon'? We introduce the notion of a belief commitment point: the token position at which the model's internal truth-value stabilizes to its final judgment. Using token-wise probing of a recovered truth direction across the reading of each proposition, we trace belief trajectories for several open-weight models. We hypothesize and test that (1) commitment onset is identifiable and often precedes the fact-determining token, (2) premature commitment (committing before the disambiguating token) predicts belief-vs-fact errors and reliance on surface heuristics better than final-token confidence, and (3) causally delaying commitment — by attenuating the truth direction at pre-disambiguation positions until the proposition is fully read — reduces premature-commitment errors while preserving factual QA. We design controlled propositions with a controllable disambiguation position (garden-path-style items whose truth flips only at a late token, versus early-decidable items), and correct-answer-flippable minimal pairs. We introduce a commitment-lead metric (tokens between commitment and disambiguation) and localize the layers/heads that drive early commitment. This reframes belief-vs-fact confusion as a reading-dynamics problem and provides a cheap, interpretable intervention. All experiments run on <=9B open-weight models feasible for an academic lab.
Experiments: 1) Dataset construction: Build propositions with a controllable disambiguation position. (i) LATE-DECIDABLE items whose truth-value is only determined by a late token (e.g., 'The capital of France is [Lyon/Paris]', 'X is visible from the [Moon/street]'), created as minimal pairs that flip truth by changing one late token. (ii) EARLY-DECIDABLE items where truth is fixed early. (iii) GARDEN-PATH items that suggest one truth-value early then reverse late. Use factual (from TriviaQA/PopQA/MMLU templates, tunable prior-strength) and neutral/fictional templates. ~2-3k items with entity/order/paraphrase randomization and single-token minimal pairs. Estimate per-item empirical answer accuracy via repeated sampling. 2) Token-wise probing: On Llama-3-8B, Qwen2.5-7B, Gemma-2-9B (plus a base-vs-chat pair), recover a truth direction via difference-of-means on a held-out true/false set. Then, for each proposition, decode the probe's truth score at every token position across layers, yielding a belief trajectory. Define the commitment point as the earliest position after which the decoded sign/score stays within a tolerance of the final value; define commitment-lead = (disambiguation position − commitment position). 3) Behavioral link: Test whether premature commitment (positive commitment-lead, i.e., committing before disambiguation) predicts belief-vs-fact errors on LATE-DECIDABLE and GARDEN-PATH items (AUC), and compare against a final-token-confidence baseline and against P(True). Measure how commitment-lead scales with prior-fact strength and garden-path strength; compare first- vs third-person and belief-vs-fact phrasings. 4) Mechanism localization: Identify layers where the trajectory first stabilizes and use attention/activation attribution to find heads that write the truth direction early; test whether early-committing heads attend to prior-consistent surface cues rather than the disambiguating token. 5) Causal delay intervention: (a) Attenuate the truth direction (project it out or scale it down) at all positions before the disambiguation token, restoring it afterward; measure whether this reduces premature-commitment errors (accuracy gain on LATE/GARDEN items) and specificity (no harm on EARLY-DECIDABLE items or unrelated factual QA). (b) Reverse control: inject the early-prior truth direction to induce more premature-commitment errors, validating the mechanism. 6) Lightweight fix: A small LoRA (or steering-only) trained to suppress early truth-direction activation until the proposition end; evaluate premature-commitment-error reduction and factual QA retention (MMLU/TriviaQA subset). Metrics: commitment-lead distribution, commitment-point localization, prediction AUC vs. baselines, per-layer trajectory stabilization, steering accuracy gain and specificity, retained factual accuracy.
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) A truth direction recovered globally may not be valid at intermediate token positions where the proposition is incomplete; mitigated by validating the probe on partial-prefix true/false sets and reporting where the probe is trustworthy. 2) Decoded intermediate scores may reflect surface-completion priors rather than genuine belief; this is partly the phenomenon of interest, but we add fictional-item controls and minimal pairs to distinguish. 3) Defining a discrete commitment point from a noisy trajectory is nontrivial; we test multiple tolerance thresholds and report sensitivity. 4) The disambiguation position must be cleanly annotated; we use single-token minimal pairs to make it unambiguous. 5) Delaying commitment via projection could have off-target effects; specificity/retention metrics quantify this. 6) Effects may vary across model families, tokenizers, and item types; we report per-condition rather than universal claims.
